description:
Check that a figure or sentence really appears in a filing document, and get a
link that highlights exactly where.

Use this before stating any number or quotation from a filing. Analysts need to see
the figure in the source; a link to the whole document is not enough. Quote the text
as it appears in the document: a sentence, or a table row's label and figure
("Total net sales 416,161", "Gross margin 75.0%"). Words and numbers must match
exactly. Spacing, table-cell breaks, "$" and curly quotes may differ.

Returns found (true/false) and, for each occurrence, its surrounding context, a
highlight_url (beatandraise.com viewer, marks that exact span, including across table
cells), to cite with the quotation. If there are several occurrences, pick the one whose context fits
the claim, or quote more of the row to pin one. If found is false, do not present the
text as a quotation from this document: numbers_elsewhere shows where its figures do
appear, which usually reveals a misremembered figure or the wrong document.

Args:
    cik: CIK of the filer (e.g. "0000320193")
    accession_number: SEC accession number (e.g. "0000320193-25-000079")
    filename: The document the text came from (e.g. "aapl-20250927.htm", or an
        exhibit such as "q4fy26cfocommentary.htm"), as listed in content_object
        or in a search result
    quote: The exact text to find (max 1000 characters)
name: verify_quote
title: Verify a Quote or Figure
